subject: [RFC PATCH v3 00/14] Introduce tiered memcg limits

reviews.author: Song Hu
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that the calculation of `penalty_jiffies` in `calculate_high_delay()` can overflow due to the multiplication of `max_overage * max_overage`, which can exceed the maximum value representable by a fixed-point number. This issue is caused by the fact that `max_overage` is calculated as `(usage - high) << 20 / high`, leading to a potential overflow when `high` is tightened far below the current usage of a large working set.
reviews.raw_body:
(pre-existing, not from this series - mentioning it here because
it reworks memory.high behaviour)

The penalty computation in calculate_high_delay() can overflow:

	penalty_jiffies = max_overage * max_overage * HZ;

max_overage is a fixed-point relative overage:
calculate_overage() returns (usage - high) << 20 / high, so the
square times HZ wraps once (usage - high) / high reaches
4096 / sqrt(HZ).  That is roughly 130x at HZ=1000 and 259x at
HZ=250 - reachable when memory.high is tightened far below the
current usage of a large working set.

Most wrapped values are still caught by the 2s clamp in
mem_cgroup_handle_over_high(), but residues below the clamp pass
through, and some of them produce far less throttling than
intended - down to no sleep at all.

check_mul_overflow() with a clamp would saturate the penalty
instead of wrapping it.  Could be folded in while memory.high is
being reworked, or a standalone fix.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in a future version.

Author acknowledges that Song Hu raised a valid concern about penalty_jiffies/throttling, but suggests that the issue is outside the scope of his patch series and proposes a standalone fix.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:21:15 +0800 Song Hu <husong@kylinos.cn> wrote:

Hi Song, thank you for your reply.

---

I think this could be a real concern, but I'm not sure that my series
is the right place to fold this change in. Namely because I don't
touch the penalty_jiffies / throttling part at all.

Maybe a standalone fix could be worth it? : -) I have no plans at the
moment so please feel free to take a crack at it if you think it's
a good idea!
Joshua

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new boot parameter 'cgroup.memory=tiered_limits' that enables tier-proportional scaling and enforcement of memory cgroup controller limits. The feature is incompatible with cgroup v1 and raises a warning if a system booted with tiered limits mounts a legacy cgroup. A static key is used to minimize overhead for cgroups not using tier-aware memcg limits, which will become a hotpath in later commits.
